notes: Klein et al., 'Atiqot 112 (2023) pp. 53-92: Murabba'at Cave II (Cavities A-E, three levels, 89 m long). The coding names the cave by its classic number, which the lane holds as Zissu's Murabba'at cave No. 2: stated identity (PLAN 4.2). Not added. No pillar, terrace, opening or facing word in the coding, so no clause would change. INFERENCE that Roman II = No. 2 of the 1952 numbering.

Hadas, 'Atiqot 46 (2004) pp. 5-14 (Hebrew; English pp. 127*-128*): a rock-cut pyrite and limonite mine in the fault-escarpment cliff near 'En Gedi spring, 15 m long, 0.9-1.1 m wide, nicknamed 'Small Pyrite Cave'. Admitted because the coding calls it a cave by name (PLAN 4.1(1); exploratory: a hewn mine, not a natural cave). No opening, pillar, terrace or facing word: C2-C5 unknown. Period: 3rd c. BCE(?), Second Temple unqualified and Mamluk, so 'partly' (PLAN 4.4). The lane holds no cave of this name.

Harding (unsigned), ADAJ 2 (1953) p. 85: 'four large caves' in Wadi Murabba'at (I and II over 50 m long), the 1952 excavation. The lane holds the same four caves, Nos. 1-4 (Zissu 2023; count from Reed 1954 p. 8): stated identity by name, number and count (PLAN 4.2). Not added. No clause word in the coding.
